questions.question: The line \( x+y=2 \) is tangent to the curve \( x^{2}=3-2 y \) at its point.
questions.explanation:
Equation of the tangent is, 

x+y=2⇒y=-x+2

So the slope of the tangent is =-1

Given the equation of the curve is, 

x2=3-2y⇒2y=3-x2

Differentiating with respect to x we get, 

2dydx=-2x⇒dydx=-x

We know that the slope of tangent to the curve y=f(x) is given by =dydx

Now, 

dydx=-1⇒-x=-1⇒x=1

Substituing the value of x in the equation of tangent, 

y=-1+2=1

The required point is (1,1).
